import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9))

# Define a color palette for sensor types for consistency
sensor_types = sorted(df['sensor_type'].unique())
palette = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(sensor_types))
sensor_palette = dict(zip(sensor_types, palette))

# Create the scatterplot
# Y-axis (price) is on a log scale to better visualize the wide distribution.
# Point size is proportional to megapixels.
# Point color is determined by the sensor type.
ax = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='model_year',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    hue_order=sensor_types, # Ensure consistent legend order
    palette=sensor_palette,
    size='megapixels',
    sizes=(30, 450), # Min and max bubble sizes
    alpha=0.75,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Set the y-axis to a logarithmic scale for better distribution visibility
ax.set_yscale('log')

# Improve the plot with a clear title, subtitle, and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Model Year, Sized by Megapixels', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=25)
plt.suptitle('Full Frame cameras consistently command higher prices, with megapixels generally increasing over time.', fontsize=12, y=0.92, color='gray')
plt.xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD) - Log Scale', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Format the y-axis ticks to be more readable (e.g., "$1,000")
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f'${int(y):,}'))
ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mticker.NullFormatter()) # Remove minor ticks for clarity

# Customize the legend to separate color (hue) and size
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# The legend is created in two parts by seaborn (hue and size). We split them.
hue_end_index = len(sensor_types) + 1
legend_hue = ax.legend(handles[1:hue_end_index], labels[1:hue_end_index],
                       bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left',
                       title='Sensor Type', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11')

# Add the size legend back to the plot as a second, separate legend
legend_size = plt.legend(handles[hue_end_index:], labels[hue_end_index:],
                         bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6), loc='upper left',
                         title='Megapixels', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',
                         labelspacing=1.5) # Increase spacing for clarity

# Add the first legend (hue) back to the plot, as the second one overwrites it
ax.add_artist(legend_hue)

# Customize grid lines
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.5)

# Set x-axis limits to be a bit wider than the data range
plt.xlim(df['model_year'].min() - 1, df['model_year'].max() + 1)

# Save the figure with a tight bounding box to include the legend
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
